current_answer: As of 5 October 2026, reviewed public evidence does not establish a broad capability decline across popular deployed models or a confirmed Claude Opus 5.5 regression. OpenAI reports elevated Work Mode errors beginning at 07:03 UTC; its 09:50 update says the issue was mitigated and recovery is being monitored for ChatGPT Work and Codex in ChatGPT Desktop. That is service evidence, not a model-quality result. Anthropic documents safety fallbacks that can change the responding Claude model on some requests; check the per-response model label and fallback notice before comparing outputs. BridgeBench’s Opus 5.5 launch-power score rose to 96.5% on 4 October from 94.2% on 2 October, within its stated 90–110% band, but combines task performance, tokens, and cost. LiveNerf reports two follow-up days after its baseline and no comparison result yet. A user’s same-prompt Godot comparison is a task-specific lead, not proof without inspected outputs and served-model records.

catalogue_card.question: Is there proof Claude Opus 5.5 was downgraded?
catalogue_card.text: No confirmed regression. BridgeBench’s launch-power score rose to 96.5% after an October 2 low, still within its own 90–110% band. The score also mixes task results, token use, and cost.

summary: OpenAI reports elevated Work Mode errors beginning 07:03 UTC on 5 October. Its 09:50 update said the issue was mitigated and recovery was being monitored; ChatGPT Work and Codex in ChatGPT Desktop were listed as affected.

Anthropic says some safety-flagged Opus 5.5 requests can be answered by an earlier model. The product displays a switch notice and labels the model that answered; record that label before comparing output.

BridgeBench’s 4 October Opus 5.5 launch-power score is 96.5%, up 2.3 percentage points from its 2 October low and within the board’s own 90–110% band. It combines task performance, tokens, and cost; tasks and weights are private.

LiveNerf reports 12 of 30 collections by 5 October, including two days in its first follow-up window. It has not published a post-baseline comparison; the first possible decision is around 24 October.
A user reports that a same-prompt Godot task produced a worse artifact on 2 October than on 23 September. The files, run logs, and responding-model identity were not independently checked.
Marginlab’s Opus 5.5 page is marked last updated 29 September and continues to say the baseline is collecting and degradation detection is paused; its rates are not a current before-and-after result.
If a familiar task fails, check the exact surface and status, capture the response-model label, prompt, files, settings, output, and correction work, then replay after recovery against your baseline.
uncertainty: BridgeBench’s launch-power score is a composite, not a capability-only measure; tasks and weights are private and its result page shows no sample uncertainty.
LiveNerf’s result will cover a fixed panel through one headless Claude Code subscription path, not all Claude surfaces or ordinary user tasks.
The Godot report is one self-reported task comparison; its output artifacts and exact served models, routes, and settings were not independently verified.

OpenAI status is aggregate and does not establish which accounts were affected or measure answer quality. The 5 October incident was mitigated and recovery was being monitored, not reported as fully resolved at the last inspected update.
No representative repeated task series across providers, first-party analytics, controlled audience pilot, or purchase evidence was available.
freshness_note: Checked 5 October 2026 at 12:13 UTC. OpenAI had mitigated a Work Mode incident and was monitoring recovery; BridgeBench’s latest Opus 5.5 test was dated 4 October; LiveNerf had two follow-up days and no comparison result.
